scope: Audit Strata's live KV-streaming and session-file boundaries, then exercise a real 112,626-token Qwen conversation save, engine restart, and restore from the B550 Optane partition. Compare that native path with Mooncake's documented Transfer Engine and Store roles.

implementation_audit.live_kv_streaming: The authoritative streamed QSA K/V is device-mapped pinned host RAM; VRAM holds a hot-cell pool. The test engine reported 32768 of 262144 cells per QSA layer in VRAM and 3.09 GiB pinned RAM. This is not a live NVMe paging tier.
implementation_audit.disk_session_files: With slot_save_path configured, Strata serializes the running state, deepest checkpoint, every authoritative QSA layer's K/V, and draft K/V. Linux moves the payload in aligned 16 MiB blocks and uses O_DIRECT when the filesystem accepts it, otherwise buffered I/O.
implementation_audit.session_file_restrictions: Session save/restore is refused with --layer-split, --peer-device, --batch (server parallel slots), or --prompt-cache 0. The successful test therefore used one GPU; the preferred two-GPU split-30 configuration cannot currently use this native file tier.
implementation_audit.mooncake: Current Mooncake documentation describes an embedded Transfer Engine (segments and asynchronous BatchTransfer across DRAM, accelerator memory, and NVMe-oF) plus Store, a distributed object pool with a Master control plane and local SSD/NVMe tiers. It is Apache-2.0, but it is not a Strata QSA-layout plug-in; a connector must map Strata blocks, fingerprints, residency, and validation to Mooncake objects.

result.native_capability: Yes for parking and restoring a whole conversation on Optane. A real 112K-token session became a 1.956 GB file in 1.463 s and restored into a new engine process in 2.232 s.
result.not_live_offload: No for a live authoritative NVMe KV tier. During inference the authoritative K/V is pinned host RAM; the Optane file is read only by an explicit restore and is not consulted by the per-token KV resolver.
result.mooncake_decision: Do not introduce Mooncake for one B550 host. Use native session files now. A Strata-native async QSA block pager is the correct local engineering step if many concurrent long sessions exceed RAM. Mooncake becomes useful only for a multi-host shared or replicated KV pool, after Strata has engine-specific block metadata and transfer semantics.
result.default_change: None. This was an opt-in measured server configuration; no deployed runtime or installer default was changed.

No continuation request was issued after restore, so output equivalence and follow-up prompt-cache savings are not newly measured here.
The logs do not state whether exFAT accepted O_DIRECT for this file; the measured number is end-to-end save/restore time with the filesystem and integrity checking included.
No live per-token NVMe paging, eviction, concurrency, layer-split session support, or multi-host Mooncake connector was implemented.
